title: Timbac 55 radish (Timbac 55 F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Timbac 55 radish is an F1 hybrid radish variety from Allied Botanical. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Timbac 55 radish is an F1 hybrid radish variety, also sold or known as Timbac 55 F1 or Timbac radish. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Timbac 55 radish is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Timbac 55 F1 or Timbac radish, this is the same radish. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [radish variety finder](/crop-varieties/radish), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit radish fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 40 to 45 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Root: big and even with a green shoulder, 250 to 400 g.
Holds very well in the field.
Intermediate resistance to pests and diseases (Allied does not say which).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: Allied Botanical's green shoulder hybrid radish for lowland to highland farms, the only evidence found is Allied's listing. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual radish on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Timbac 55 radish

Labanos is fast. Pick a variety that stays crisp and does not turn pithy in the heat. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Fertilizer for vegetables](/blog/fertilizer-for-vegetables-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Timbac 55 F1 the same as Timbac 55?
items.a: Yes. Timbac 55 F1 is another name for Timbac 55. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Timbac 55?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
